rationale: Sources extend upward and rightward in their own colours. In demonstration 1, 5 stops immediately to its right at 3; in demonstration 2, 4 extends upward only until the 3.
Demonstration 1 extends 2, 7 and 3 vertically in their own colours. In demonstration 3, 1 paints downward but its upward ray is blocked immediately by 9.
Sources paint all four diagonals in their own colours. In demonstration 1, the diagonal from 1 overwrites 8 at row 2, column 2, and diagonals from 7 overwrite both adjacent 9 pixels.
Demonstration 2 extends 4 along its full row and column, overwriting the 9 pixels in its column. Demonstration 3 preserves source pixels 5 and 2 while their vertical rays cross.
The 5 sources in demonstration 1 paint vertical rays of 4, stopping before 8. In demonstration 3, the downward ray from 5 stops before the first 9, leaving cells below both 9 pixels unchanged.
Demonstration 1 fills background cells in the row containing 1 and 6 with 4. Demonstration 3 paints on both sides of the 9 in the bottom 6 source's row while preserving that 9.
Demonstration 1 paints 4 downward from 2 and 3, preserving source 3 and overwriting 8 below it. Demonstration 2 extends downward from 1, 3 and 6 without painting above them.
Demonstration 2 produces diagonal rays of 4 from 3 and 6. Demonstration 3 stops the down-right ray from 6 before source 4 and the up-left ray from 7 before 9.
Demonstration 1 extends 6 only to the left in colour 6; demonstration 2 similarly extends both 7 sources, and demonstration 3 extends 1. Colours 8 and 9 emit no rays.
Demonstration 1 extends 4 rightward and downward in colour 4. In demonstration 3, the rightward ray from the lower 6 stops before 8 at the row's right edge.
